Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

hvtiRpropensity 0.2.2

  • The README’s Installation section now leads with hvtiR::install(), which installs the whole HVTI R family in one call, and then gives pak::pak("ehrlinger/hvtiRpropensity") for this package alone.

hvtiRpropensity 0.2.1

0.2.1 fixes formula handling across the model functions and the findings of a rollup review of the 0.2.0 series. Two changes move published numbers; check them before upgrading a study:

  • Pooled degrees of freedom are Barnard and Rubin’s, as mice::pool() reports them, so pooled p-values and intervals change.

  • Ordinal standard errors come from the expected information, as SAS reports them, so ordinal p-values and intervals change, by a fraction of a percent on the package’s test data.

  • fit_logistic() accepts a dot formula such as y ~ .. It stopped with “Required column(s) not found in data: .” before. The dot expands to every column except the outcome, id_col and imputation_col, as it already did in bs_continuous() and fit_linear().

  • bs_count() checks outcome_col the way bs_continuous() does: a value that is not the formula’s response, or a response naming more than one column, is refused. A dot formula no longer fits the id_col and imputation_col columns as covariates.

  • fit_logistic(), fit_linear(), bs_continuous() and bs_count() check only the predictors the model keeps. A variable the formula subtracts, as in y ~ . - dropme, is no longer checked for matching levels across imputations, and fit_logistic() no longer lists it in $meta$predictors.

  • fit_linear(), bs_continuous() and bs_count() require the response to read exactly one column even when outcome_col is supplied. I(count + other) with outcome_col = "count" fitted the sum while recording count as the outcome; cbind(count, other) stopped with an unhelpful subscript error.

  • Pooled estimates from fit_logistic(), fit_linear(), bs_continuous() and bs_count() use Barnard and Rubin’s (1999) small-sample degrees of freedom, with complete-data degrees of freedom n - k, as mice::pool() does. They used Rubin’s (1987) large-sample degrees of freedom, which can run into the millions when little is missing. The df column, and the p-values and intervals built on it, change for every pooled model; estimates and standard errors do not. A coefficient with no between-imputation variance, which had infinite df and a normal test, now gets a finite df. To reproduce the values in SAS, run PROC MIANALYZE with EDF= set to n - k. The help pages for all four functions explain the calculation under “Pooled degrees of freedom”.

  • Pooling over imputations stops with an error when the first imputation’s model has no residual degrees of freedom (n - k of zero or less), as a saturated model does. A saturated pooled logistic model returned meaningless df and p-values before.

  • The SAS oracle fixtures for fit_logistic() and fit_linear() now include a PROC MIANALYZE EDF= run, and the tests check the pooled degrees of freedom, p-values and intervals against it directly. No change in behaviour.

  • ps_forest() accepts a dot formula such as tavr ~ .. It stopped with “Required column(s) not found in data: .” before. The dot expands to every column except the treatment and id_col, as it does in ps_logistic(). A column the formula subtracts, as in . - x3, is no longer fitted, checked for missing values or reported in the SMD table.

  • ps_logistic(), ps_ordinal() and ps_nominal() leave a constant column the formula subtracts out of the SMD table.

  • The SAS oracle fixtures for fit_logistic() and bs_count() are exported at full precision, with the PROC LOGISTIC fits run at GCONV=1e-12. The binary, nominal and pooled comparisons, and the PROC GENMOD Poisson comparison, are tested at tolerances near their measured agreement. No change in behaviour.

  • fit_linear(), bs_continuous(), bs_count() and ps_forest() check every column the formula names, subtracted ones included, as fit_logistic() does. A subtracted column missing from data reached lm() or glm() as “object not found”, or picked up a same-named object from the calling environment; in ps_forest() a misspelled one was ignored, so the column meant to be dropped was fitted.

  • bs_count() refuses a transformed response such as log(count + 1), which it fitted as counts with a warning. fit_logistic() refuses one too, matching its error message.

  • A . that leaves no columns once the response, id_col and imputation_col are set aside stops with a clear error.

  • Ordinal models in fit_logistic() and ps_ordinal() report standard errors from the expected (Fisher) information, as SAS PROC LOGISTIC does, instead of MASS::polr()’s observed information. The two differ for the cumulative logit; on the package’s SAS oracle data the standard errors moved by up to 0.4%, and the p-values, intervals and pooled results with them. vcov() on the stored polr() model still returns the observed version.

  • polr() runs at a tighter tolerance (reltol = 1e-14), so ordinal estimates move slightly (about 2e-5 on the oracle data) and now agree with SAS to about 1e-7.

hvtiRpropensity 0.2.0

0.2.0 consolidates the work since 0.1.0 and the fixes from a rollup review of that series (#79 to #93). Before upgrading a study, check these changes, each described in full below:

  • The four sa_*() functions return ps_data objects; results move into $meta and $tables.

  • sa_evalue() needs rare = TRUE or FALSE for an odds ratio or a hazard ratio, and its earlier conversions were the wrong way round.

  • ps_rmst() on a ps_match() object analyses the matched pairs and resamples them by pair; score weighting of a matched object is refused.

  • Weighted SMDs normalise the weights within each arm, so they no longer depend on stabilise and can differ from SAS %stddiff when the weights do not average 1.

  • ps_forest() writes matching weights, not overlap weights, to mt_wt.

  • ps_ordinal() needs an ordered factor or treatment_levels.

  • ps_weight() stabilises ATE weights only.

  • Rows with a missing treatment or score are excluded and counted, not crashed on or silently kept.

  • DESCRIPTION now declares the Quarto command line tool in SystemRequirements. The vignettes have always needed it to build; the field makes that visible to installers and to R CMD check.

  • Articles on the pkgdown site put the table of contents on the left and use the full width of the window, through pkgdown/extra.css. The installed vignettes are unchanged: the Quarto vignette engine renders them in its own minimal format, which has no sidebar layout.

  • ps_match() gains scale = c("probability", "logit") and caliper_sd, so pairs can be matched on the logit of the propensity score with a caliper in pooled standard-deviation units, sqrt((var_t + var_c) / 2). scale = "logit", caliper_sd = 0.2 is the Austin (2011) recommendation. The default stays "probability", which keeps the [0, 1] check on score_col. $meta now records scale and caliper_sd, and $meta$caliper is the absolute caliper applied.

  • The SAS templates in inst/sas-templates/ no longer carry the study they were taken from: each study path is now /studies/<study>, and the study title and cohort line read <study description> and CCF, 19xx to 20xx, n=xxxx, as the %let STUDYDESC and %let STUDYPOP lines already did. The analysis code is unchanged.

  • fit_linear() fits an ordinary least-squares model to one dataset or to stacked imputations, with Rubin-pooled inference verified against PROC MIANALYZE. It returns the same data, models, meta and tables shape as fit_logistic(), and its $tables$fit_quality gives each fit’s residual standard error and R-squared. A single fit, here and in bs_continuous()’s new estimates, is inferred on the t distribution with residual degrees of freedom, as PROC REG reports it. A dot formula such as ef ~ . expands over the data’s columns excluding the identifier and imputation columns, here and in bs_continuous(), so the patient ID is never fitted as a covariate.

  • bs_continuous() now carries fit status, coefficient estimates, covariance and per-imputation estimates, as bs_count() does. Its balancing score is unchanged. A transformed exposure, such as log(hct_nadr) ~ ..., now works.

  • bs_continuous() now stops, naming the imputation, when a term is aliased (for example a covariate that duplicates another), where it used to return a score from a rank-deficient fit.

  • The pooled-covariance check against PROC MIANALYZE in test_lm_sas_oracle.R now compares like with like. SAS’s TCov is the multivariate total covariance, (1 + rbar) * Ubar, not the elementwise Rubin total that fit_logistic() reports, so the test checks the diagonal against the SAS standard errors and rebuilds TCov from the per-imputation fits, at 1e-5 rather than 1e-4. No package code changed.

  • The help pages for ps_match(), ps_weight() and the package now name hvtiPlotR::hv_mirror_hist() and hvtiPlotR::hv_balance() as code rather than linking to them. ‘hvtiPlotR’ is not a declared dependency, so R CMD check could not resolve the links on a machine without it and reported “Unknown package ‘hvtiPlotR’ in Rd xrefs”.

  • Behaviour change: ps_forest() now writes Li-Greene matching weights (ATM; Li & Greene, 2013) to weight_col (default mt_wt), min(p, 1 - p) / p for treated patients and min(p, 1 - p) / (1 - p) for controls, exactly as ps_logistic() does. It previously wrote overlap (ATO) weights, 1 - p and p, under the same name, so swapping one scoring function for the other silently changed the estimand. Anyone who read mt_wt from a ps_forest() result, for weighted balance, ps_mw_var() or hvtiPlotR::hv_mirror_hist(weight_col = "mt_wt"), gets different weights and should rerun. Both help pages now state the estimand (#83).

  • Behaviour change: ps_ordinal() now stops unless the treatment is an ordered factor or treatment_levels gives the level order. It used to order a character or unordered-factor treatment alphabetically, so "Low"/"Medium"/"High" was fitted as High < Low < Medium, with no warning and coefficients of the wrong sign. The error says how to declare the order (#87).

  • ps_logistic() with treated_level alone now accepts any treatment with two values, such as a "TAVR"/"SAVR" factor, as ps_forest() already did, and gives the same scores as the 0/1 coding. A treatment with more than two values still stops (#87).

  • ps_logistic(), ps_ordinal(), ps_nominal(), fit_logistic() and fit_linear() check id_col only when imputation_col is set, as their documentation says. Data without an id column no longer stops a single-dataset fit (#87).

  • ps_stddiff() now normalises the weights to mean 1 within each group before computing a weighted Gaussian or rank difference, so multiplying a group’s weights by a constant no longer changes it (#82). As a result ps_weight()$tables$smd_weighted is the same with stabilise = TRUE and stabilise = FALSE, and ps_stddiff_perm() with weight_col inherits the fix.

  • Weighted SMDs change for Gaussian and nong_ord variables whenever the weights do not already average 1 in each group, as matching weights and unstabilised IPTW weights do not. They then no longer equal the %stddiff macro’s output, which depends on the scale of the weights; they still equal it when the weights average 1 in each group. Binary and categorical differences, and every unweighted difference, are unchanged.

  • sa_evalue() now applies the odds-ratio and hazard-ratio conversions the right way round (VanderWeele & Ding 2017). For a rare outcome the OR or HR is used as the risk ratio directly; for a common outcome the OR becomes sqrt(OR) and the HR becomes (1 - 0.5^sqrt(HR)) / (1 - 0.5^sqrt(1/HR)). Earlier versions always took the square root, which understated the E-value for a rare outcome (an OR of 2.5 gave 2.54 instead of 4.44).

  • Behaviour change: sa_evalue() gains a rare argument, and a call with type = "OR" or "HR" now aborts unless it sets rare = TRUE or rare = FALSE. Rarity is the outcome’s prevalence in the study population (under about 15% at the end of follow-up) and is not inferred from p0, which is used only for type = "RD". The returned list records the choice as $rare. The function also aborts unless ci_lo <= estimate <= ci_hi.

  • ps_rmst(), ps_support(), sa_overlap() and sa_trim_sweep() now back-transform the score of a ps_match() object built with scale = "logit" with plogis(), so its weights, trim rule and overlap diagnostics are on the probability scale. Before, they read the logit as a probability: ps_rmst() clipped it to [0.001, 0.999], ps_support() trimmed logits at 0.1 and 0.9, and the two sa_*() functions stopped with a range error (#80). ps_support() and ps_rmst() record $meta$scale, carried from their input, so a chain such as ps_rmst(ps_support(matched), ...) still reads the logit correctly.

  • ps_match() warns when scale = "logit" is given a score column whose every value lies in [0, 1], which is most likely a probability such as the default prob_t. Its [0, 1] range error now suggests scale = "logit" for a logit score.

  • NEWS.md corrections: the 0.1.0 entry now lists all sixteen initial exports, and the 0.1.8 ps_forest(), 0.1.9 group_counts and 0.1.11 seed entries no longer claim more than the code did. Each correction is dated in place (#92).

  • The default covariates of the balance tables in ps_weight(), ps_match(), ps_logistic(), ps_nominal() and ps_ordinal() now leave out the id column, the treatment and score columns, the columns this package appends (prob_t, logit_t, mt_wt, iptw, match, pair_id, quintile, decile, bs, cluster, and the prob_<level> scores ps_nominal() and ps_ordinal() generate) and constant columns. A predictor named in the model formula is always kept. Before, id and match appeared in the ps_weight() table of sample_ps_data(), and prob_t in a ps_match() table matched on logit_t. A covariates vector you supply is used unchanged (#85).

  • ps_weight() gains id_col = "id", as ps_match() has, so the identifier stays out of its balance tables.

  • fit_logistic() checks that ‘MASS’ (ordinal) or ‘nnet’ (nominal) is installed before it fits, and the tests that use either package skip when it is absent (#89).

  • The test suite and the ps_forest() example cap ‘randomForestSRC’ at two cores (#89).

  • ps_rmst() on a ps_match() object now analyses the matched pairs only, so n is twice the number of matched pairs, and its bootstrap resamples whole pairs by pair_id instead of rows. A matched input runs "unweighted" by default and refuses score weighting, which would adjust twice. Earlier releases used every row of the cohort and ignored the pairing. $meta$resampling records "pair" or "row".

  • ps_rmst() on a ps_weight() object now uses its stored weight column for the scheme that matches its estimand ("ate" or "att"), so trimming is kept, where it used to recompute the weights from the score. $meta$stored_weighting names that scheme.

  • ps_rmst() now stops when tau is past the last observed time in either arm of an analysed subset, counting only rows that enter the weighted curve (time and event present, weight above zero), where it used to carry the last survival value forward. The help page now also says that failed bootstrap draws are counted in n_failed and that refit = FALSE intervals ignore the uncertainty in estimating the score.

  • ps_weight() now stabilises weights by the marginal treatment probability for estimand = "ATE" only. For "ATT" and "ATC", stabilise has no effect, so treated weights under the ATT and control weights under the ATC are exactly 1, as documented; before, the default stabilise = TRUE scaled them by the arm’s marginal probability. $meta$stabilised records whether stabilisation was applied, and sa_trim_sweep() follows the same rule. ATE weights are unchanged (#88).

  • ps_match() accepts only the number 1 for ratio. ratio = 1.5 and ratio = "1" were silently accepted and now stop with an error naming the value (#88).

  • ps_support() stops when a flags element is named "trim" or "common", which the built-in rule silently overwrote, and when trim is not two increasing probabilities in [0, 1] (#88).

  • An NA in caliper or caliper_sd (ps_match()) or trim (ps_weight(), ps_support()) now stops with an error naming the argument instead of “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” (#88).

  • Rows with a missing treatment or a missing score are now excluded and counted rather than crashing or misleading (#84). ps_match() leaves them out of the treated and control pools, ps_weight() gives them a missing weight and leaves them out of the stabilising proportion and the balance tables, and ps_support() computes the common-support interval on the remaining rows and gives them missing flags. Each states the count in one warning and records it in $meta$n_excluded. ps_support() also works with a single rule (trim = NULL or common = FALSE).

  • ps_logistic() counts a patient with a missing treatment out of group_counts, the strata and the balance tables, keeps their predicted score, says so in one accurate warning, and records the count in $meta$n_missing_treatment.

  • fit_status now reports the rows a model dropped for every family. ps_nominal() and fit_logistic(family = "nominal") reported none, because nnet has no nobs() method.

  • bs_continuous() and bs_count() give a missing balancing score missing strata instead of ranking it into the top stratum, and need id_col only when imputation_col is set.

  • Breaking change: sa_rosenbaum(), sa_evalue(), sa_overlap() and sa_trim_sweep() now return ps_data objects of classes sa_rosenbaum, sa_evalue, sa_overlap and sa_trim_sweep, with the four slots $data, $meta, $tables and $models, a print() method each, and the shared summary(). Code that read the old lists reaches the same values here:

    • sa_rosenbaum(): res$bounds is res$tables$bounds; res$sensitivity_value and res$n_pairs are res$meta$sensitivity_value and res$meta$n_pairs. The pairs used are in the new res$tables$pairs.
    • sa_evalue(): evalue_estimate, evalue_ci, rr_estimate, type and rare move under res$meta, and res$tables$evalue holds both E-values as a table. res$data is an empty data frame.
    • sa_overlap(): summary, outside_overlap and positivity_flags move under res$tables, and overlap_region under res$meta.
    • sa_trim_sweep(): the data frame it returned is res$tables$sweep.

  • Breaking change: the four sa_*() functions follow one rule for arguments a ps_data input already records. A supplied argument that disagrees with the object’s $meta now aborts, naming both values, where it used to be silently overridden: sa_rosenbaum(m, "ef", treated_level = 0), sa_trim_sweep(w_ate, estimand = "ATT") and sa_overlap(m, score_col = "other") all abort. An argument not supplied takes the metadata, then its default. sa_rosenbaum() now also reads pair_id_col from the metadata.

  • sa_rosenbaum() corrects its variance for ties, using the sum of squared average ranks in place of n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. Without tied absolute differences the bounds are unchanged; with ties they change slightly. At Gamma = 1 the bound now equals the one-sided wilcox.test() p-value with exact = FALSE.

  • sa_rosenbaum() gains alternative = c("auto", "greater", "less"). The default "auto" keeps the earlier results, picking the direction from the sign of the median difference; the documentation now says so, and that Rosenbaum’s method assumes the direction is fixed in advance.

  • sa_overlap() excludes patients with a missing treatment as well as those with a missing score, and sa_trim_sweep() excludes patients with a missing score, with a warning giving the count, so the effective sample sizes and pct_trimmed are computed on the analysed rows (part of #84).

  • Tests now assert what their names claim: the caliper, trim = NULL, estimand and stabilised-weight tests are pinned to hand-computed values, the imputation test checks prob_t against the mean of the per-imputation fits, the AUC test uses wilcox.test() as an independent oracle, and the sa_trim_sweep() tests reach the estimand and machine-epsilon paths they name. No package code changed (#93).

  • The help pages now list everything each function returns (#90). fit_logistic(), validate_logistic(), ps_logistic(), ps_ordinal(), ps_nominal() and bs_count() name every $data column, $meta field, $tables entry and their $models; ps_match() and ps_weight() add treated_level, and ps_match() says that n_unmatched counts unmatched treated patients only. fit_logistic() documents the choices for family and the role of id_col.

  • ps_logistic(), ps_ordinal(), ps_nominal() and fit_logistic() describe their handling of multiple imputation correctly: per-patient probabilities are averaged across imputations on the probability scale, the “across” approach of Leyrat et al. (2019), and not Rubin’s rules, which pool only the coefficients. $data and the balance table use the lowest-numbered imputation’s covariates. ps_logistic() gives the “within” recipe that Leyrat et al. recommend.

  • The help pages name the estimand: ps_match() the ATT, narrowed by a caliper to the treated patients who could be matched; ps_weight() the ATE, ATT or ATC; ps_mw_var() with the matching weight the ATM; and ps_support() says that trimming changes it.

  • Corrections: ps_logistic()’s matching weight mt_wt feeds neither ps_match() nor ps_weight(); ps_stddiff() no longer calls ps_weight()’s weights matching weights; ps_forest() lists its own $meta; ps_mw_var() cites Li and Greene (2013) with its DOI; sample_ps_data_count(n_imputations > 1) says that it draws independent patients per imputation; and a stray backtick no longer breaks the treatment_col entry of sa_overlap() and sa_trim_sweep().

  • The vignette’s hvtiPlotR examples now run. hv_mirror_hist() takes column names as strings (score_col, group_col, match_col, weight_col) and returns a data object for plot(). hv_balance() does not read $tables directly: it needs one long data frame with variable, group and std_diff in percent, and the vignette now shows the reshape. The package help and the README no longer say the tables feed it as they are. ‘hvtiPlotR’ is now in Suggests (#91).

  • The vignette now covers ps_forest(), ps_stddiff(), ps_stddiff_perm(), ps_mw_var(), ps_rmst() on matched pairs, ps_support(), matching on the logit with caliper_sd = 0.2, and the rare argument sa_evalue() needs for odds and hazard ratios. Every ps_match() call in it gives a seed. It no longer says all four sa_*() functions measure unmeasured confounding: sa_overlap() and sa_trim_sweep() check positivity and overlap.

  • The README quick start runs: it weighted a data frame whose score column it had just removed. Its status block now says which parts SAS oracles check (since 0.1.10), and its function tables list all 25 exports.

  • The package help page lists all 25 exports, says which return ps_data objects (all but the four data generators and is_ps_data()), and points to the SAS programs shipped in system.file("sas-templates", package = "hvtiRpropensity").

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.11

  • A seed now makes every random function reproducible whatever the session drew before it. ps_forest(), ps_match(), ps_rmst(), ps_stddiff_perm() and ps_mw_var() set the stream to abs(seed) immediately before their draws and restore the caller’s stream afterwards. ps_forest() now does this as well as passing seed = -abs(seed) to randomForestSRC::rfsrc(); before, it set no R seed. The default stays seed = NULL, which draws from the caller’s stream as before. A positive seed gives the same result as in 0.1.10, except in ps_forest(), whose 0.1.10 result depended on the session’s earlier draws; a negative one now gives the same result as its absolute value. (Corrected 2026-10-13: the original entry did not exempt ps_forest().)
  • Each of those five functions records the seed it used in $meta$seed, NA when none was given. ps_stddiff_perm() and ps_mw_var() used to store NULL there. A seed that is not one whole number is an error.
  • ps_forest() documents the thread trade-off: if two runs with the same seed disagree, set options(rf.cores = 1L).
  • A new test scans every function in the package and fails on a random draw that no seeding call precedes.
  • sample_ps_data(), sample_ps_data_ordinal(), sample_ps_data_nominal() and sample_ps_data_count() no longer warn when called with seed = NULL. NULL now draws from the caller’s random-number stream, as ps_match() and ps_rmst() do, so set.seed() before the call reproduces the data. Before, the generators reseeded from the clock and warned that .Random.seed was NULL.
  • The generators now check seed and use its absolute value, as the five functions above do: a negative seed gives the same data as its absolute value, and a seed that is not one whole number is an error.
  • Now requires R 4.4.0 or newer, up from 4.1.0, to match the rest of the HVTI family. hvtiR::install() installs the members together, and several already required 4.4.0, so on an older R the install failed whatever this package declared.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.10

  • New tests compare ps_stddiff(), ps_stddiff_perm() and ps_mw_var() with the CCF macros %stddiff, %stddiffci and %mw_var, run in SAS on a synthetic dataset (tests/testthat/fixtures/stddiff-sas/). All three agree with the macros: standardized differences to within 4e-7, the %mw_var estimate to 3e-10 (#34).
  • New treated_level argument on ps_match(), ps_weight(), ps_stddiff(), ps_stddiff_perm(), ps_mw_var(), sa_overlap(), sa_trim_sweep() and sa_rosenbaum(). It names the treated value, so the treatment column may hold any two values (for example "surgical" and "transcatheter"), as ps_logistic() already allowed. Results equal those from the same data coded 0/1, the group tables show the study’s own level names, and $data keeps the column as it was given. ps_forest() accepts such a column through its existing treated_level. The default, NULL, keeps the 0/1 or logical requirement, so existing calls are unchanged (#60).
  • sa_overlap(), sa_trim_sweep() and sa_rosenbaum() read the treated level from a scored or matched object, so an object scored with treated_level = 0 is no longer analysed with the arms swapped.
  • sa_trim_sweep() and sa_rosenbaum() now check the treatment column. A column that is not 0/1 or logical used to be coerced with warnings and return a result; it is now an error unless treated_level is given.
  • sa_trim_sweep() excludes patients whose treatment is missing, with a warning. It used to keep them, which made every effective sample size NA.
  • The group tables of ps_match(), ps_weight(), ps_forest() and sa_overlap() no longer label the groups control and treated. group now holds the value in treatment_col (0/1, or FALSE/TRUE), and a new logical treated column says which group is treated, as in ps_logistic(). Code that matched group == "treated" should use the treated column (#51).
  • ps_ordinal() and ps_nominal() now return a balance table, $tables$smd, as ps_logistic() does. It has one row per covariate and pair of treatment levels (variable, level, versus, smd), each computed on the patients in those two levels. A new smd_pairs argument chooses the pairs: "reference" (default) compares each level with the reference, "adjacent" (ordinal only) compares each level with the one below it, and "all" compares every pair. The choices can be combined (#48).
  • ps_rmst() now defaults to seed = NULL, as ps_match(), ps_stddiff_perm() and ps_mw_var() already did. The default was seed = 1024L, which gave the same bootstrap draws on every call. A call that relied on the default now gives an interval that varies from run to run; pass seed for a reproducible one. Point estimates are unchanged.
  • sample_ps_data_count(seed = NULL) no longer errors and returns a fresh dataset, as the other three generators did. The generators keep their fixed default, seed = 42L, so that examples share one demo dataset (#53).
  • fit_logistic() and validate_logistic() have examples.
  • The examples for ps_ordinal(), ps_nominal() and ps_rmst() run only when the suggested package they need (‘MASS’, ‘nnet’, ‘survival’) is installed.
  • The package help no longer says sa_rosenbaum() requires ‘rbounds’. It never did: the bounds are computed in base R.
  • DESCRIPTION spells out CORR and SMD, quotes ‘hvtiPlotR’ and cites Rosenbaum and Rubin (1983). Help pages use ASCII punctuation in place of em dashes and arrows (#53).

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.9

  • ps_match(), ps_rmst() and the sample_ps_data*() generators restore the caller’s random number stream when they return. Each called set.seed() and left the stream reseeded, so everything the caller drew afterwards depended on the seed passed here. They now use withr::local_seed(), as ps_stddiff_perm() and ps_mw_var() already did. Results for a given seed are unchanged.
  • bs_count() and other count-family models now name the exponentiated coefficient column rate_ratio. It was labelled odds_ratio, but the exponent of a log-link Poisson or negative-binomial coefficient is a rate ratio. Binary, ordinal and nominal models keep odds_ratio (#46).
  • ps_logistic()’s $tables$group_counts names each row by the declared treatment level instead of control/treated, and adds a logical treated column. (Corrected 2026-10-13: the original entry said this made it read the same as ps_ordinal() and ps_nominal(), whose group_counts have group and n only.) Without treatment_levels the groups are 0/1 (or FALSE/TRUE) (#47).

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.8

  • New ps_forest(): out-of-bag random-forest propensity score in a ps_data object (needs the suggested randomForestSRC). (Corrected 2026-10-13: the original entry said it had the same contract as ps_logistic(), but its mt_wt held overlap weights rather than matching weights, and its $meta and $tables lack the model-bundle fields.)
  • New ps_support(): flags weak-support patients under common-support, score-trimming and user-supplied rules (e.g. isolation-forest tails) and tabulates pairwise agreement (kappa, Jaccard).
  • New ps_rmst(): observed-outcome restricted mean survival contrast from weighted Kaplan-Meier curves with a stratified bootstrap interval; its $tables$estimates / $tables$curves feed hvtiPlotR RMST plots.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.7

  • ps_ordinal() now creates its documented rank-based quintile and decile columns from the averaged probability of the highest ordered treatment level, including for stacked imputations. Existing columns with either name are rejected instead of overwritten.
  • bs_count() bundles now record their bundle version, count-model family and R/package versions, matching the saved-model metadata contract introduced in 0.1.6.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.6

  • Adds fit_logistic() for binary, proportional-odds ordinal, and nominal generalized-logit model bundles, including explicit outcome-level contracts, retained per-imputation fits, averaged patient predictions, and Rubin-pooled coefficients and covariance.
  • Adds validate_logistic() for calibration, observed-versus-expected events, AUC, and Brier validation of a saved version-1 binary bundle without refitting or modifying it.
  • Existing binary, ordinal, and nominal propensity functions and count balancing scores retain their scored columns and diagnostics while gaining fitted models, inference, covariance, and fit-status tables. Negative-binomial bundles also retain theta for every imputation.
  • Stacked-imputation workflows now require the same patient keys in every imputation. They error on missing patients instead of silently averaging a patient’s score over fewer imputations.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.5

  • ps_mw_var() estimates a matching-weight treatment effect with a bootstrap variance, ported from the CCF %mw_var SAS macro (Rajeswaran 2014, after Li and Greene 2013). For each outcome it reports the PROC MEANS weighted mean, SD and sum of weights by group, the difference, and from n_rep replicates resampled within each group the bootstrap SD, PCTLDEF=1 percentiles (quantile(type = 4)), z and p. As in the macro the weights are held fixed across replicates, so the SD ignores the uncertainty in estimating them; the documentation says so. The macro’s output labelled the sum of weights N, reported here as sumwgt_0 and sumwgt_1.

  • withr moves from Suggests to Imports. ps_stddiff_perm() and ps_mw_var() take a seed and restore the caller’s random number stream afterwards, through withr::local_seed(). Restoring the stream by hand means writing .Random.seed in the global environment, which R CMD check reports as a NOTE.

  • ps_stddiff_perm() gives each standardized difference a permutation reference, ported from the CCF %stddiffci SAS macro (Artis 2020). It reports the observed ps_stddiff() value beside the 2.5, 16, 50, 84 and 97.5 percentiles of the same statistic over n_perm shuffles of the group labels, using SAS PCTLDEF=5 (quantile(type = 2)), the macro’s PROC UNIVARIATE default. The percentiles describe what label shuffling alone produces, not a confidence interval. Weights that depend on the group are recomputed for every permutation by a reweight function, which is required with weight_col; the macro instead expected those permuted weights to exist as columns already. A seed makes the result reproducible and leaves the caller’s random number stream as it was.

  • ps_stddiff() computes standardized differences for every variable type, ported from the CCF %stddiff SAS macro (Artis 2019): Gaussian, non-Gaussian or ordinal by pooled ranks, binary, and categorical by Yang and Dalton’s Mahalanobis form, each optionally weighted. It returns a ps_stddiff object whose $tables$stddiff holds one row per variable. The denominator averages the two group variances as the macro does. A categorical variable whose groups share no levels gets NA with a warning. Design: hvtiRtemplates dev/specs/2026-09-16-standardized-difference-design.md; tracked in #34.

  • The SMD tables from ps_match(), ps_logistic() and ps_weight() now come from ps_stddiff(), and their numbers change. Every covariate is treated as Gaussian, as before, but the denominator is now the macro’s sqrt((var1 + var0) / 2). The unweighted tables (smd_before, smd_after, smd, smd_unweighted) used to pool the SD by sample size, which differs whenever the groups are unequal, so smd_before is the table most likely to move; with equal groups it does not. The weighted table (smd_weighted) used to divide its variances by sum(w) and now divides by n - 1, as PROC MEANS does. The tables keep their variable and smd columns and 4-place rounding. A covariate named in covariates must now be numeric; a character column used to yield NA with a warning and now stops.

  • ps_weight() stops with a clear error when a propensity score of exactly 0 or 1 gives an infinite weight, naming the count and pointing to trim. It used to fail later with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed” from inside the SMD calculation. With trim set, the infinite weight is winsorised as before and the call succeeds.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.4

  • Fixes an empty changelog on the pkgdown site. NEWS.md opened with a bare # hvtiRpropensity title line, so level one was the title level and every version heading sat at level two. pkgdown reads the top heading level in the file as the version level, found no versions there, and warned “no version headings found” on every build. That title line is removed and the four version headings are promoted to level one, matching the rest of the family. A level-one heading that names no version, such as the (unreleased) one above, is skipped by pkgdown rather than counted, so it does not reintroduce the problem. utils::news() was unaffected throughout and still reports the same four versions.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.3

  • Removed the explicit Maintainer: field from DESCRIPTION and moved the maintainer address to john.ehrlinger@gmail.com in Authors@R, matching the rest of the hvtiR* family. The two fields had disagreed: Authors@R named the ehrlinj@ccf.org address while Maintainer: named the gmail one, which R CMD check --as-cran reported as a note. Maintainer: is now derived from the cre role at build time, so the two cannot drift apart again.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.2

  • Qualified the rnorm() calls in the sample_ps_data*() generators as stats::rnorm(), matching every other statistics call in the package, and declared stats under Imports. This clears the R CMD check note about an undefined global function. Generated data is unchanged: the seeds and the RNG draw order are identical.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.1

  • Renamed from hvtiPropensityScores into the hvtiR* package family (hvtiRtemplates, hvtiRutilities, hvtiRlifetables, hvtiRtables). No user-facing function names or behaviour changed.

hvtiRpropensity 0.1.0

  • Initial development scaffold.
  • (Added 2026-10-13: the original 0.1.0 entry listed four exports. These were exported too: ps_logistic(), ps_ordinal(), ps_nominal(), bs_continuous(), bs_count(), sa_rosenbaum(), sa_evalue(), sa_overlap(), sa_trim_sweep(), sample_ps_data_ordinal(), sample_ps_data_nominal() and sample_ps_data_count().)
  • Added sample_ps_data(): reproducible synthetic cardiac-surgery dataset.
  • Added ps_match(): greedy nearest-neighbour 1:1 propensity score matching without replacement, with optional caliper.
  • Added ps_weight(): IPTW weighting supporting ATE, ATT, and ATC estimands, with optional stabilisation and weight winsorisation.
  • Added is_ps_data() predicate and print / summary S3 methods for the common ps_data base class.
